cities.base: Downtown/Gemmayze area for walkability and dinner options
cities.name: Beirut

cities.base: Old town near the port and castle
cities.name: Byblos

places.name: Downtown Beirut
places.note: Rebuilt after the civil war and the port blast, so it reads more like a stage set than a living quarter.

places.name: The Corniche
places.note: Seafront promenade, best around sunset when everyone comes out to walk.

places.name: Mar Mikhael / Gemmayze
places.note: Dinner and bar-hopping street, the anchor for a Beirut evening on foot.

places.name: National Museum of Beirut
places.note: Small but the mosaics and sarcophagi are worth the hour and a half.

places.name: Jeita Grotto
places.note: Upper and lower cave system; confirm Monday closures before you build the morning around it.

places.name: Harissa cable car and viewpoint
places.note: Cable car up to the Our Lady of Lebanon statue with coastal views.

places.name: Baalbek Temple Complex
places.note: The best Roman ruin site in the country, the scale is what makes the two hours each way worth it.

places.name: Anjar Umayyad ruins
places.note: A half-hour add-on to Baalbek, the weaker of the two sites, skip if you're tired.

places.name: Beiteddine Palace
places.note: Druze palace, hours roughly 9-4 but it sometimes closes for events so confirm before you go.

places.name: Deir el Qamar
places.note: Old stone village next to Beiteddine, the natural lunch stop for that day.

places.name: Byblos Old Town
places.note: Small enough to wander without a plan.

places.name: Byblos Crusader Castle
places.note: Compact ruin overlooking the port, an hour is enough.

places.name: Batroun seafront
places.note: Fish dinner by the water, the evening half of the Byblos travel day.

places.name: Cedars of Lebanon
places.note: Ancient cedar grove at 2000m, cold even in July so bring a jacket.

places.name: Gibran Museum
places.note: Housed in a former monastery, dedicated to Kahlil Gibran.

places.name: National Museum of Beirut
places.note: Small but well curated, Phoenician and Roman mosaics and sarcophagi, good rainy day option, some pieces were hidden in concrete during the civil war which is its own story worth reading on the wall text.

places.name: Downtown Beirut and Martyrs' Square
places.note: Rebuilt Ottoman/French-era core around Nejmeh Square, half glossy restoration half still-scarred buildings, the Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque and nearby Maronite cathedral sit a block apart, worth a walk more than a lingering sit.

places.name: Corniche Beirut (Ain El Mreisseh to Raouche)
places.note: Seafront promenade, best at sunset when everyone in the city seems to be out walking, fishing, or drinking coffee from a cart, leads naturally to Pigeon Rocks.

places.name: Raouche (Pigeon Rocks)
places.note: The city's postcard rock formation, free to view from the clifftop cafes, boat rides out to the arch are touristy and skippable unless the sea is very calm.

places.name: Mar Mikhael / Armenia Street
places.note: Bars and small restaurants along Armenia Street, the district that carries Beirut's reputation for nightlife despite the 2020 port blast damage next door, quieter than pre-2020 but still the best evening strip.

places.name: Gemmayze (Rue Gouraud)
places.note: Steep street of old sandstone houses, bars, and small galleries, walkable straight from Downtown, some buildings still under repair from the port explosion.

places.name: Sursock Museum
places.note: Restored Ottoman-Venetian villa turned modern art museum, badly damaged in the 2020 blast and reopened after repair, free entry, check hours as they've been irregular since reopening.

places.name: Zaatar w Zeit or a corner manoushe bakery (Hamra branch)
places.note: Manoushe with zaatar or cheese fresh off a saj, this is the cheap honest Beirut breakfast, chain is fine but a standalone furn is better if you spot one.

places.name: Tawlet Souk el Tayeb
places.note: Daily changing lunch buffet cooked by a rotating home cook from a different Lebanese region, a genuine way to eat food you would not get in a restaurant, lunch only, closed Sundays.

places.name: Hamra Street
places.note: Beirut's old intellectual and commercial spine, bookshops, cafes, AUB campus nearby, less polished than Downtown and more lived-in.

places.name: American University of Beirut (AUB) campus and Museum
places.note: Green, quiet campus above the sea, the small AUB Archaeological Museum is free and one of the oldest museums in the Middle East, a good calm break from street noise.

places.name: Place de l'Etoile clock tower photo stop
places.note: Skip lingering here, it is the same clock tower photo everyone takes and the surrounding streets are often barricaded or empty depending on the political mood, the rest of Downtown nearby is more worth your time.

places.name: Byblos Crusader Castle
places.note: 12th century fort built from reused Roman columns, climb the tower for a view over the harbor and the ruins field around it. Uneven stone stairs, wear real shoes.

places.name: Byblos Archaeological Site
places.note: Same ticketed grounds as the castle, layers of Phoenician, Roman and Bronze Age remains stacked together. Little shade, go before midday in summer.

places.name: Byblos Old Souk
places.note: Narrow stone lanes between the castle and the port, small shops selling crafts and jewelry rather than a working produce market. Pleasant to wander, not essential.

places.name: Byblos Old Souk Fishing Port
places.note: Small stone harbor still used by fishing boats, a few cafes along the water. Good for a sunset walk after the castle closes.

places.name: Memory of Time Fossil Museum
places.note: Small private collection of fish fossils from Lebanon's quarries, good rainy-hour filler near the castle, not a full outing on its own.

places.name: Church of St John the Baptist
places.note: Crusader-era church next to the castle, plain and quiet inside, worth the five minute detour on the way between the ruins and the souk.

places.name: Feniqia Byblos
places.note: Small cultural center walking through Phoenician heritage and the origins of the alphabet, aimed at families, skippable if you're short on time.

places.name: Sur Mer
places.note: Long running seafood restaurant built into the rock right on the water by the old port, order by weight, go for sunset.

places.name: Feiruz Byblos Cafe
places.note: Small coffee stop on the way into the souk, fine for a break between the ruins and the harbor, nothing that needs a special trip.

places.name: Batroun Corniche and Old Souk
places.note: Coastal town twenty minutes north of Byblos, old souk lanes, the Phoenician sea wall, and a run of bars and seafood spots along the water, good for a dinner evening out of Byblos.

places.name: Colonel Restaurant Batroun
places.note: Seafront fish restaurant in Batroun's old town, straightforward grilled fish and mezze, works well as the day 5 evening stop on the way into Byblos.

places.name: Byblos Wax Museum
places.note: Skip: dated dioramas of Lebanese history and folklore, worn figures, better spent at the actual castle and ruins next door.

places.name: Jeita Grotto Upper Cave
places.note: Walkway through dry limestone chambers, no photos allowed inside, the formations are genuinely huge, gets crowded with school groups by midday. Confirm Monday closure before building the morning around it.

places.name: Jeita Grotto Lower Cave Boat Ride
places.note: Included in the same ticket as the upper cave, a short flat-bottomed boat glide through the underground river, closes seasonally when water levels are high so check on arrival rather than assume it's running.

places.name: Jeita Cable Car
places.note: Short cable car connecting the parking and entrance area to the upper cave level, included in general admission, more a convenience than an attraction in itself.

places.name: Nahr al-Kalb (Dog River) Inscriptions
places.note: Cliff-face carvings and plaques left by passing armies over 3000 years, Egyptian, Assyrian, Roman, French, a few minutes off the coastal highway between Beirut and Jeita, easy to fold into the drive.

places.name: Harissa Teleferique
places.note: Cable car up from Jounieh's seafront to Harissa, good views over the bay on a clear day, lines build up on weekends and holidays.

places.name: Our Lady of Lebanon Shrine, Harissa
places.note: Bronze Marian statue on a hilltop platform, pilgrimage site for Lebanese Christians, the terrace view over Jounieh Bay is the actual draw for most visitors.

places.name: Jounieh Seafront Corniche
places.note: Promenade along the bay below the cable car station, casual, mostly locals in the evening, decent spot to sit before the drive back to Beirut.

places.name: Casino du Liban
places.note: Large casino and cabaret complex north of Jounieh, dated and pricey, only worth it if gambling specifically is the point, otherwise skip in favor of Beirut nightlife.

places.name: Chez Sami, Jounieh
places.note: Long-running seafood spot on the Jounieh waterfront, mezze and fresh fish, a reasonable lunch stop between the grotto and Harissa rather than doubling back to Beirut hungry.

places.name: Nahr Ibrahim / Adonis Valley Viewpoint
places.note: Scenic gorge further up the coast road, only makes sense if extending the day north toward Byblos rather than as a stop on a Beirut-Jeita-Harissa loop, skip unless the schedule has slack.

places.name: Roadside Manoushe Stop, Jeita Highway
places.note: Generic but real category rather than one named bakery, small manoushe and saj stands line the highway near the grotto turnoff, a quick zaatar or cheese wrap before the cave visit costs almost nothing.

places.name: Jounieh Old Souk
places.note: Small covered market street behind the seafront, low-key, mostly clothes and household goods, a five minute wander if waiting for a table rather than a destination in itself.

places.name: Téléphérique Jounieh-Harissa
places.note: Cable car up from Jounieh seafront to Harissa, about 10 minutes each way with views over the bay. Gets busy on weekends, and it closes in high wind, so have a backup plan.

places.name: Our Lady of Lebanon Shrine (Notre-Dame du Liban)
places.note: Bronze Virgin Mary statue on a hilltop, the destination the cable car is built for. Free to visit, small chapel underneath, and the terrace around the statue gives the best coastal view in the area.

places.name: Maronite Basilica of Saint Paul and Saint Peter
places.note: Modern concrete basilica next to the shrine grounds, built in a style meant to echo a boat hull. Worth a quick look if you are already there, not a destination on its own.

places.name: Harissa hillside viewpoint near USEK
places.note: Roadside pullouts along the ridge above Jounieh with unbroken views down to the coast, quieter than the shrine terrace and a good spot for photos without the crowd.

places.name: Jounieh Seaside Corniche
places.note: Waterfront promenade at the base of the cable car, good for a walk before or after going up to Harissa. Nothing remarkable in itself but it fills the gap either side.

places.name: Chez Sami
places.note: Long-running seafood restaurant on the Jounieh waterfront, popular with locals for a sit-down lunch before or after the cable car. Not cheap by Lebanese standards but reliable.

places.name: Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) grounds
places.note: Campus at the base of the Harissa hill with a small museum of Lebanese heritage. Only worth the stop if you have spare time, it is not a headline sight.

places.name: La Maison de Vin Harissa area cafes
places.note: Cluster of small cafes near the shrine terrace with coastal views, fine for a coffee stop while waiting for a cable car queue to clear rather than a destination of its own.

places.name: Our Lady of Lebanon Museum
places.note: Small museum below the shrine covering the site's history and religious artifacts. Skippable unless it is raining and you have already done the statue and basilica.

places.name: Casino du Liban
places.note: Landmark casino building north of Jounieh with a storied history through the civil war years. Only worth a stop if you gamble or want the building's history, otherwise skip.

places.name: Maameltein Bay waterfront
places.note: Quieter stretch of Jounieh Bay north of the main marina, decent for an evening stroll with fewer crowds than the central Corniche.

places.name: Jounieh Marina and waterfront restaurants
places.note: Row of restaurants and cafes along the marina, a straightforward option for dinner after coming down from Harissa in the evening light.

outings.why: The grotto is the big cave system north of Beirut, then the Harissa cable car and viewpoint round out the day; door to door about 5 hours including traffic out of the city.
outings.name: Jeita Grotto and Harissa cable car
outings.season: year-round, confirm Monday hours before committing the morni

outings.why: Baalbek is the best Roman ruin site in the country, about 2 hours each way via Chtaura; Anjar's Umayyad ruins are a half-hour add-on and the weaker of the two, skippable if tired.
outings.name: Baalbek and Anjar

outings.why: A half-day round trip to the Druze palace with lunch in the adjacent village; hours roughly 9-4 but it sometimes closes for events so confirm first.
outings.name: Chouf: Beiteddine Palace and Deir el Qamar

outings.why: A full day up to the cedar groves and the Gibran Museum in Bcharre, 2 hours up and 2 back plus time at altitude; cold at 2000m even in summer, bring a jacket.
outings.name: Cedars of Lebanon and Bcharre
outings.season: best in summer for road access; cold year-round at altitude

destination.name: Lebanon
destination.pitch: Beirut plus day trips: Roman ruins, a Druze palace, and Byblos, without much circulation driving.
destination.caveat: The US State Department has Lebanon at "reconsider travel," tied to the Syrian border, the south, and Hezbollah-influenced areas, which is why this itinerary stays Beirut-based rather than pushing east or south. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Beirut on foot covers Downtown, the Corniche, and Mar Mikhael/Gemmayze for dinner.
because.food: Manoushe in Beirut, fish dinners on the Batroun seafront.
because.nature: Jeita Grotto and the Cedars of Lebanon at 2000m, cold even in summer.
because.culture: Baalbek is the best Roman ruin site in the country, plus Anjar's Umayyad ruins and Beiteddine's Druze palace.
because.exploration: Byblos old town and its Crusader castle, plus Bcharre and the Gibran Museum.
